key_insight: Se/ZnMgO photodiodes act as self-powered visual synapses whose weight change direction is controlled by light wavelength: short-wavelength light potentiates while longer-wavelength light depresses the response.
engineering_relevance: This enables zero-bias, optically programmable synaptic devices for neuromorphic vision hardware, with energy-free read/write and flexibility-compatible operation.
method: Built Se/ZnMgO thin-film photodiodes that use zero-bias photocurrent as the synaptic state.
Compared wavelength-dependent updates under 365 nm and 455 nm light at equal photon flux.
Used optical simulations and drift-diffusion modeling to link plasticity to interface defect filling and light penetration depth.
evidence_signal: At equal photon flux, 365 nm pulses increased photocurrent by 38% while 455 nm pulses decreased it, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch; a digit-recognition network reached 89% accuracy without noise and 85% with measured noise.
watch_item: Performance depends on interface defect population and stored states can be erased by reverse bias or sub-gap light, so device consistency and ambient-light robustness need careful control.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
